question: Ticket bec37ac3ae5d says "measured addresses are stored as 'repo/<path>', 'commons/<path>', 'instance/<path>' using root names 'repo', 'commons', 'instance' in a simplified 'name/path' format", but outline 17.28.1.1 reads "cairn:/// is the repo (from the environment, or from where bin/cairn itself lives); cairncommons:/// is the commons repo beside it; instance:/// is ~/.cairn; claude:/// is ~/.claude (the project's own .claude/ is already cairn:///.claude/, so it gets no second name); db:///cairn/table/row is the database; file:/// keeps its usual meaning, a real path on the filesystem, for what no root holds. claude: is also the Claude app's link scheme on this box: the resolver never hands an address to the system, so only a click on one opens the app." (17.28.1.1 prescribes that rooted addresses use the scheme format 'cairn:///', 'cairncommons:///', 'instance:///' with specific root names and the :/// structure. The ticket's format omits the scheme syntax and uses different root names, contradicting the specified addressing standard for rooted addresses.). Which stands, the ticket or the outline?
why_it_blocks: the ticket and the component outline disagree; building it would build one of them wrong
answer: The outline stands. 17.28.1.1 already names rooted addresses as dataref schemes (cairn:///, cairncommons:///, instance:///), and cairn/tools/dataref/dataref.py resolves them; the ticket's 'repo/<path>' form was a re-derivation of a settled address. Ticket rewritten: measured is stored as a dataref address and the proof resolves it back through Dataref.
